name: listing-table
purpose: A titled preview of a longer listing: a few linked rows in columns, and one outlined button into the full list. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'listing-table', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `section-title`, `frame-box`, `table` and, below `sm`, `item`. Each row is one link named by its first column; the whole row is clickable with the pointer and the first column's link is the keyboard and screen-reader path. Below `sm` the same rows become a list of items, the first column as the title and the second as the description, with the button going full width.
useWhen: To preview the latest entries of a listing (open roles, releases, events) with a way into the full list.
avoidWhen: For a filterable or paginated listing → use `listing-browser`.
For a comparison of plans or features → use the pricing matrix.
related: table` — the composition table the wide layout renders.
listing-browser` — the full listing this band links into.
bestPractices: Keep three columns at most; the first names the row and the second describes it on phones.
Give the wide columns `grow: 2` and align a short trailing column to `end`.
Keep the preview to a handful of rows and point `primaryAction` at the full listing.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it.

props.name: title
props.doc: Headline of the band, rendered by the left-aligned section title as its `h2`; the band renders no header when empty.

props.name: columns
props.doc: The columns left to right; each is `{ key, label, grow?, align? }` where `key` picks the row value, `grow` is the flex weight (1, 2 or 3) and `align` is `start` or `end`. The first column names the row and the second describes it on phones.

props.name: rows
props.doc: The linked rows, in order; each is `{ href, values }` where `values` maps a column key to its text.

props.name: primaryAction
props.doc: Outlined button into the full listing, in the table footer; `{ label, href, trailing? }` where `trailing` adds the chevron. Omitted when absent.

examples.name: Default
